subject: Fiscal Year 2023 Medford Public Schools Budget
overview: The Committee met with school administrators to review the proposed $69 million fiscal year 2023 school budget and its impact on staffing and programs. The Council approved a motion requesting that the Mayor restore school funding for educator retention using recently updated ARPA revenue estimates.

items.title: Fiscal Year 2023 School Budget Presentation
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent presented the $68,994,776 recommended budget, noting that it required strategic compromises and limited staff non-renewal notices to balance against the Mayor's allocation. The administration stated that while the budget is balanced, it relies on shifting personnel items to one-time grant and revolving fund sources.

items.title: Discussion of Budget Gap and Funding Sources
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Murphy detailed the $2.8 million difference between the School Committee's initial request and the executive recommendation, explaining that most priority initiatives were moved to grant funding or deferred. Councilors questioned the sustainability of using one-time federal ARPA and ESSER funds for recurring personnel costs.

items.title: Curriculum, Staffing, and Student Services
items.summary: Councilors inquired about potential increases in teachers' out-of-pocket costs for supplies, the 37% enrollment spike in English learner programs, and persistent challenges in filling paraprofessional positions. The administration outlined plans for new math coaches and expanded mental health counseling funded through temporary grants.

items.title: Vocational Programs and Security Infrastructure
items.summary: Administrators provided updates on high-interest vocational programs such as electrical and culinary arts and discussed security measures including door monitors and school resource officers. Concerns were raised regarding the adequacy of maintenance funding for school buildings and security camera upgrades.

items.title: Legal Counsel and Settlement Reporting
items.summary: Councilor Knight questioned the role and cost of the School Committee's dedicated legal counsel and requested a full report on recent legal settlements and their funding sources.

items.title: Motion to Restore School Funding
items.summary: Approved a motion requesting that the Mayor utilize increased ARPA revenue replacement estimates to appropriate additional funding for educator retention and collective bargaining negotiations.

items.title: Executive Response on Fiscal Strategy
items.summary: Chief of Staff Nina Nazarian clarified that the Mayor intends to reduce the city's reliance on one-time funds to align recurring costs with recurring revenues as federal pandemic aid expires.
